title: Weighted Random Choice
statement:
Choose a value randomly according to positive weights.

Contract
- `values` and `weights` are non-null, have the same positive length, and every weight is positive and finite.
- Use the supplied `Random`; do not create another source of randomness.
- The probability of returning `values[i]` is `weights[i] / sum(weights)`.
- Return one of the provided values.

Examples
- With values `[10, 20, 30]` and weights `[1, 3, 6]`, `30` is most likely.
- With one value `[7]`, the result is always `7`.
- Equal weights choose uniformly among the values.
hints: Think of the weights as adjacent ranges on a number line.
Draw a random threshold between zero and the total weight.
Walk the ranges until the cumulative weight passes the threshold. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
inputSyntax: Input: values then a semicolon then weights, for example: [10, 20, 30]; [1.0, 3.0, 6.0]
